notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); this package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null), and no hardware was attached or run.

WHAT IT SERVES: the card's models[0], resources/robots/pai_12dof/mjcf/pai_12dof.xml, as a MujocoDriver in simulated mode. The card's entry symbol humanoid/scripts/sim2sim.py:89 run_mujoco(policy, cfg) was confirmed in the clone and is cited as a Fact; it loads the MJCF (line 100), creates MjData (line 102) and steps it (line 172). Importing sim2sim also imports humanoid.envs and therefore Isaac Gym (humanoid/envs/base/legged_robot.py:36-37), so this package serves the model itself, not that script. cap.world.step.v1 takes {ticks, action: {ctrl: [...]}}; each ctrl element is checked by the bridge against the model's actuator_ctrlrange (twelve elements of -200..200 from pai_12dof.xml:153-164) before data.ctrl is written, then mj_step runs ticks times. cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults with mj_resetData + mj_forward. The state is the bridge's integration state (time_ms, qpos, qvel, ctrl, tick, timestep_ms, seed); the fake derives nq=19, nv=18, nu=12 and timestep 1 ms from the same MJCF. The card's second model, resources/robots/pai_12dof/mjcf/pai_12dof_terrain.xml, is not served: one package serves models[0].

WHY THIS SHAPE: the card's helper is MujocoDriver (family-config), which matches a MuJoCo model. MuJoCo is not installed and cannot be installed where the gate runs (no network, no pip), so backends['fake'] is this package's stand-in mujoco module in fake.py (the form other MuJoCo family packages use). It is a callable factory, so the lock names the import path .fake:fake_mujoco while the class holds the callable. The stand-in parses the same MJCF text for the joint dimensions, the per-actuator control ranges and the option timestep, but integrates a placeholder joint motion proportional to each control value; it loads no mesh and resolves no contact, friction, equality, tendon, actuator or sensor dynamics. The fidelity contract therefore declares F0 (the deployed fake has no dynamics) while noting that the MJCF and real MuJoCo would support F1, and its gaps list every difference. The sim backend that imports real mujoco was not run.

RISK: R1, the class MHS/spec/04-safety.md section 2.1 gives simulation stepping; the card floor R0 is met. A simulated device has no hardware backend; the runtime's software e-stop latch refuses further steps and resets until mhs.safety.reset. No estop_physical_ref is claimed and no operator-required bound is needed: the control envelope is the model's own actuator_ctrlrange.

NOT COVERED: the upstream sim2sim policy inference, observation stacking, PD torque computation, terrain model, viewer and Isaac Gym training stack (humanoid/scripts/sim2sim.py:116-176) are not part of this driver; only the MJCF world is served. No trajectory was compared with real MuJoCo or with a physical Pai robot, and no hardware was attached or run.

WARNINGS (none failed): G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND, because the fake backend is a callable stand-in for the mujoco module rather than a package class the gate can wrap in a Recorder, so the gate does not check the fake surface against the upstream entry (a function) and does not record native calls; G8.NO_UNIT x3 for ticks, action.ctrl[*] and seed, the integer/numeric inputs the simulator family derives and that PLAYBOOK.md section 8 calls expected. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was raised.

TESTS: test_driver.py keeps mhs.testing.check_driver and adds six cases (model shape from the card model, per-actuator control-range refusals with zero effect, state following the control target, reset, published fidelity contract, e-stop latch); they pass. No catalogue_requests: the package uses only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1.
